title: Pineview Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Initial discovery on Pineview's data residency and compliance requirements. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for regulated banking workloads. Key concerns: EU data residency for GDPR, US data locality for financial regs, audit/logging retention and redaction, KMS/HSM integration, and scope of PHI/hypothetical HIPAA applicability. Redwood AE/SE committed to send SOC2/GDPR docs, compliance matrix, and to schedule a technical deep dive for private deployment with Pineview's infra team.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
GDPR and EU data residency requirements
HIPAA applicability and PHI handling for banking
next_steps: Ava to send SOC2 + GDPR + ISO summary and Pineview compliance matrix (by 2026-05-04)
Diego to schedule 90-min technical deep dive for Private deployment with Samir and infra team (target week of 2026-05-11)
Pineview to share sample logs and a redaction/PII policy doc for evaluation (by 2026-05-08)
Follow-up pricing for Dedicated pilot (3-month reserved capacity) to be provided by AE
action_items: Ava Chen | Send SOC2 report, GDPR whitepaper, and compliance matrix | 2026-05-04
Diego Morales | Schedule private deployment technical deep dive (90 min) with Samir & infra | 2026-05-11
Samir Patel | Share sample application logs and PII redaction policy | 2026-05-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Marcus Lang (CTO, Pineview), Elena Ruiz (Head of Compliance), Samir Patel (Cloud Architect)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, Marcus, Elena, Samir, appreciate you making time. I'm Ava from Redwood, with Diego our SE. We'll run through a quick intro then drill into your data residency and compliance needs.
[00:18] Marcus Lang: Thanks Ava, yeah we'll keep this focused. We're evaluating options for LLM inference for customer support automation and fraud detection, but data residency and auditability are blockers.
[00:34] Diego Morales: Great, quick high-level: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Hosted is fastest to go live but has constraints we can discuss re: residency. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with SLA and capacity guarantees. Private gives you full control — your keys, network, e.g., in your VPC or on-prem.
[00:56] Elena Ruiz: Important bit for us — anything touching EU customer data needs to stay in EU for GDPR. Also, we have to produce audit trails for regulators; retention windows and the ability to redact or avoid storing certain PII are critical.
[01:12] Samir Patel: And from infra side, we need KMS integration for key control, preferably HSM-backed, and the ability to rotate keys without downtime. Also interested in log formats — we push logs into Splunk and need structured audit logs.
[01:31] Ava Chen: Understood — GDPR, retention, redaction, KMS integration, Splunk compatibility. Quick question: are you considering mixing EU and US workloads or will this be primarily EU-resident data?
[01:45] Marcus Lang: Mixed. Customer base is mainly US but we have a sizeable EU customer subset. For EU customers we must ensure data residency and, ideally, processing inside EU. For US data, we have stricter internal retention for financial transactions.
[02:01] Diego Morales: Ok — two patterns we often see: 1) Use Hosted for non-sensitive workloads and Dedicated or Private for regulated EU/finance workloads; or 2) Private across-the-board for customers who want uniform control. Hosted can sometimes be regionally isolated if the model variants and infra are available in the region, but there are limits around log retention and access to raw transcripts depending on config.
[02:26] Elena Ruiz: Can you clarify that — "limits around log retention"? We need to know what Redwood stores by default, who can access logs, and whether they contain full request/response text.
[02:38] Ava Chen: Yes. By default, Hosted collects operational logs and some telemetry; full request/response can be configured to not be stored. For enterprise customers we offer options to disable transcript storage, or store only anonymized metadata. For Dedicated and Private, you can choose retention and whether logs are shipped to your S3 or retained in your account only.
[03:02] Marcus Lang: So for Dedicated, logs are isolated — but are they still accessible to Redwood support? We need SOC2-level assurances plus an audit trail showing access.
[03:15] Diego Morales: For Dedicated we limit Redwood access and can put strict role-based access controls. Support actions are logged and require permissions. We can provide SOC2 reports and a detailed access log schema. For Private, Redwood typically doesn't have access to customer data unless the customer opts into a managed support session.
[03:36] Elena Ruiz: HIPAA — not a primary law for us but some of our partners may send PHI in claims data. How does Redwood handle PHI? Is there BAA capability?
[03:48] Ava Chen: Redwood has BAA support for Private deployments and, in some cases, Dedicated under contract. We do not recommend sending PHI to Hosted unless under a specific contract and with appropriate controls. We'll follow up with legal.
[04:04] Samir Patel: On technical notes — if we go Private in our AWS account, how does deployment work? Do you provide an AMI or helm chart? We run EKS and use K8s operators.
[04:16] Diego Morales: We have a Private package that includes Helm charts for EKS and standard docker images. There are options for on-prem as well. The control plane can be customer-managed or hybrid. Installation requires outbound connectivity for control plane, but we have air-gapped options too.
[04:36] Marcus Lang: Air-gap is big for some parts of our infra — if we need an on-prem air-gapped deployment, what are the limitations?
[04:44] Diego Morales: Air-gapped is supported for a licensed Private package. You'd run the inference runtime and optional control plane locally. It limits remote support and observability; we ship a compliance bundle and offline upgrade tooling.
[04:58] [00:05:00] Elena Ruiz: About GDPR subject requests: we need to be able to delete traces of a subject from logs and model cache. Can you evict cached KVs for a user session?
[05:12] Diego Morales: Good question. We support per-session KV cache eviction for Private and Dedicated setups. For Hosted we can provide tenant-scoped cache controls but not always per-request unless instrumented. We also have approaches to pseudonymize or hash identifiers before ingestion.
[05:33] Marcus Lang: Ok. Regarding encryption — at rest and in transit we require AES-256; we also want customer-managed keys. Does Redwood support external KMS?
[05:45] Ava Chen: Yes — for Dedicated and Private you can integrate your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM can be used for the key wrapping layer. For Hosted, we offer managed keys by default but can arrange CMK for enterprise customers.
[06:05] [00:06:10] Samir Patel: What about model artifacts — if we fine-tune or upload proprietary models, where do those live? We cannot have model weights leave our VPC for certain workloads.
[06:22] Diego Morales: For Private, model artifacts remain in your environment. For Dedicated we can provision model storage in a customer-owned bucket or a dedicated storage that has restricted access. For Hosted, model artifacts are in Redwood control plane; for proprietary models we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:45] Elena Ruiz: Logging retention periods — regulator may ask for 7 years in some litigation cases. Is that feasible? Also, redaction: can we mask account numbers and do pattern-based redaction before any logs leave our environment?
[07:00] Ava Chen: Retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; 7-year retention can be supported if your storage plan covers it. Pattern-based redaction can be done client-side (recommended) or via ingest hooks in Private; we provide prebuilt redaction plugins for common PIIs. Hosted can do configurable retention but redaction before storage is limited unless the customer sends pre-redacted payloads.
[07:27] [00:07:45] Marcus Lang: Audit trail access — we need immutable logs that show who accessed what and when. Are support actions in Redwood audited?
[07:36] Diego Morales: Yes — support actions are logged with operator ID, IP, and timestamps. For Dedicated we can export those logs to your SIEM. For Hosted we provide audit log exports for enterprise tiers. We'll share the schema.
[07:49] Elena Ruiz: One more — data residency proof. Regulators ask for proof that data stayed within borders. Can Redwood provide location attestations and time-stamped evidence?
[08:02] Ava Chen: We can provide region-level attestations showing which region processed a request and which model instance. For Dedicated and Private it's straightforward; for Hosted we can provide region logs and infrastructure attestations although some model shards might be in different zones depending on capacity. We'll clarify the exact guarantees in the compliance packet.
[08:24] [00:08:50] Samir Patel: Network controls — we need private peering between our VPC and the inference fleet, and control plane traffic restricted to specific IP ranges. Is that supported?
[08:36] Diego Morales: Yes — for Dedicated we can arrange VPC peering or PrivateLink. For Private it's by definition inside your VPC. Control plane restrictions and IP allowlists are available for enterprise setups.
[08:48] Marcus Lang: Performance tradeoffs — if we strictly keep everything in EU and use Dedicated, will we see latency or model version limitations compared to global hosted infra?
[09:01] Diego Morales: Slight tradeoffs sometimes — model catalog in-region depends on whether the open model has been benchmarked and compiled for that hardware. We maintain regional model caches but very large models may have more constrained availability. We can do pre-warm model pools for Dedicated to hit latency SLOs.
[09:18] [00:09:30] Elena Ruiz: OK, what about legal/process questions — does Redwood sign DPA with GDPR clauses and can you take on data processor obligations?
[09:28] Ava Chen: Yes, Redwood will sign a DPA and act as data processor. We'll add standard EU SCCs as needed. For specific controller-controller relationships we can coordinate legal teams.
[09:41] Marcus Lang: Can you share previous bank references or case studies for financial services?
[09:47] Ava Chen: Yes — we have anonymized case studies and references; I can share a redacted bank case study that covers deployment architecture and compliance posture.
[09:58] Diego Morales: Quick technical note — for regulatory audits we can provide a playback of access logs and config snapshots to show who changed what and when.
[10:08] [00:10:30] Samir Patel: One operational ask — we use Splunk and Datadog. How are logs formatted? JSON lines with standardized fields?
[10:17] Diego Morales: Logs are JSONL with fields for request_id, model_id, region, timestamp, operator_id, and event_type. We can adapt field names for Splunk ingestion and ship via forwarders or S3.
[10:30] Elena Ruiz: On the subject of deletion, can Redwood provide a certificate of deletion for a subject if requested under GDPR?
[10:39] Ava Chen: For Private/Dedicated we can provide deletion proof if we control the storage lifecycle; we can produce an audit record and a deletion certificate showing object keys and timestamps. For Hosted we'll need to scope the deletion capability and follow the contract.
[10:58] [00:11:15] Marcus Lang: Let's talk timeline — we're targeting a pilot for EU-regulated traffic by Q3. We want a small dedicated pilot for 3 months to validate latency and cost. What would you recommend?
[11:26] Ava Chen: I recommend a Dedicated reserved pilot with a small GPU pool in the EU region. That lets you keep logs and keys isolated while still getting Redwood managed runtime. Diego can scope the GPU types and concurrency based on your expected RPS.
[11:42] Diego Morales: If you share expected throughput and sequence lengths, I can propose batching/quantization configs to hit cost targets. Also we can run a short benchmark with sample payloads.
[11:56] Samir Patel: We'll share throughput numbers and sample requests. We also need to know pricing for a 3-month Dedicated reservation and any setup costs for Private if we choose to go that route.
[12:08] Ava Chen: I'll include pricing in the follow-up. Setup fees vary for Private vs Dedicated. We'll put together both options.
[12:18] [00:12:40] Elena Ruiz: Regarding access controls: do you support SSO, SAML, SCIM for provisioning? Role-based access?
[12:27] Diego Morales: Yes — enterprise SSO via SAML/SCIM, SSO providers like Okta, Azure AD. Fine-grained RBAC is available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted enterprise tier supports RBAC as well.
[12:40] Marcus Lang: Any encryption at-rest caveats we should be aware of for model KV cache?
[12:47] Diego Morales: KV cache is encrypted at-rest; for Private you manage the encryption keys. For Dedicated you can provide a CMK for storage encryption.
[12:58] [00:13:20] Ava Chen: Quick note about metrics: Redwood Console provides per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns and you can send traces to your tracing backend as well.
[13:07] Samir Patel: Good. On compliance docs — can you send SOC2 Type II and any ISO certs you have?
[13:13] Ava Chen: Yes — SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, and our GDPR DPA template. I'll include those in the follow-up.
[13:23] Elena Ruiz: We'll need a red team/pen test summary if available.
[13:27] Ava Chen: We have summary reports we can share under NDA.
[13:33] [00:13:55] Marcus Lang: Ok let's recap next steps so we can close the loop.
[13:40] Ava Chen: Recap: 1) I'll send SOC2/ISO/GDPR docs + privacy/compliance matrix and a redacted FS case study; 2) Diego will schedule a 90-min Private deployment technical deep dive; 3) Pineview shares sample logs and throughput numbers; 4) I'll send Dedicated pilot pricing and a proposal for the 3-month reserved capacity.
[14:05] Samir Patel: That matches our notes. Also include details on KMS/HSM integration steps and air-gap limitations.
[14:12] Ava Chen: Will do. Anything else?
[14:15] Elena Ruiz: One last question: how do you handle third-party subprocessors — where are they located and are they on your DPA?
[14:23] Ava Chen: We'll provide a subprocessors list; most are cloud infra providers and are covered under our DPA. I'll attach that.
[14:33] [00:14:55] Marcus Lang: Cool. Thank you all. We'll aim to get the sample payloads and logs to you by next week.
[14:41] Ava Chen: Thanks Marcus, Elena, Samir. We'll follow up early next week with the docs and schedule the deep dive. Appreciate your time.
[14:50] End of call.
